muted-strong.displayName: Strong Mut (the legibility floor — 7.06:1 on surface)

muted.displayName: Mut (decoration and non-essential metadata only — 3.4–3.9:1 on this ramp)

canvas.displayName: Canvas (the app ground, set on body and theme-color)

surface.displayName: Surface (cards, sidebar, top bar, tab bar, sticky footers)

paper.displayName: Paper (inputs, chips, the leading card, hollow marks)

ok.displayName: Taken Blue (deliberately identical to the accent; no green in the system)

danger.displayName: Rose Red (red severity, missed doses, P1, the alert card)

highlight.displayName: Marker Yellow (the app-wide ::selection ground, and the transcript highlighter)

display.purpose: The one hero line per screen, in Newsreader — the next medicine's name on Home. The largest thing on the screen it appears on.

headline.purpose: Newsreader at 30px: the reassurance line when every dose is accounted for, and hero quotes in QuoteBlock.

title.purpose: The lead line of a card — the alert reason, an empty-state title.

body.purpose: Default, set on body. Secondary body drops to 14px in muted-strong; metadata to 13px.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked 11px in muted-strong: section labels, card-header timestamps, tab captions. 11px exists only for these.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Every Card at rest, plus the sidebar's patient card. Warm-tinted so it never goes blue-grey on cream.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The single card that leads a screen — carried by Card emphasis="border". Two lifted cards on one screen means neither leads.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default settling easing. State changes 150ms; card shadow cross-fade 200ms; the .kv-rise entrance 340ms.

motion.name: kv-rise
motion.purpose: Card entrance on Home, so the screen settles rather than snaps. Collapsed by prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
Kinvox is a paper record of a parent's day, kept warm. The whole app sits on a cream ground (Palette F, "Cornflower & Cream" — the name is in index.css) with exactly one blue accent, and everything on it reads like entries in a ledger the adult child can trust: doses confirmed, calls made, and — above everything — the parent's own words, verbatim, in quotation marks. The user opens this app anxious; the design's job is that a calm day looks calm (whitespace and one reassuring sentence) and a bad day is loud and unmistakable (the alert card leads the Home screen and owns the full width), on the same layouts.

The recurring motif is the line: one hairline is the call connecting a child in one city to a parent in another. It is the wordmark's underline, the spine of the day thread, the severity spine on a quote, and the rule between sections. Depth comes from stepped cream tones and hairline borders far more than from shadow; the two shadows that exist are warm-tinted (rgba(58, 44, 20, …)) so they never go blue-grey on cream.

The form language is softer than a ledger usually is. Cards are generously rounded (16px) and buttons and chips are fully round — the record is warm stationery, not a spreadsheet. Radius carries hierarchy: the further a surface is from the content, the softer it gets.

This is a medical-adjacent product with a safety posture: the system never decorates meaning into colour alone, never invents a score, and never pretends the app itself can dial a phone.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream neutral ramp (11 steps, ink → paper), one blue accent, status colours only ever layered on marks that already have shape and a text label.
IBM Plex Sans everywhere; Newsreader serif reserved for care content (verbatim quotes, medicine names, hero lines, the wordmark); IBM Plex Sans Devanagari bound via :lang(hi) / :lang(mr) / :lang(pa).
Exactly three status marks — filled, outlined, muted — reused for doses, delivery, steps, radios and checkboxes.
Fully round buttons and chips; 16px cards; 6px inputs. Rounder than a form, softer than a dashboard.
Two warm shadows; borders and tone-steps do most of the depth work.
Settling motion, 150ms for state and 340ms for entrances, never springy; prefers-reduced-motion collapses everything.
Density that matches the moment: same screen, calm and loud renderings.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: One blue. Emphasis comes from weight, border thickness and whitespace, not from new hues. If a surface feels flat, add space or a border — never a colour.

rules.name: The Shape-First Status Rule
rules.body: Colour is layered onto a mark that already carries shape and a text label. Every screen must survive DevTools → Rendering → Emulate vision deficiency → Achromatopsia, and a greyscale screen recording.

rules.name: The No-Green Rule
rules.body: "Taken" is the accent blue (ok ≡ accent), never green. Good news in this system is calm, not celebratory.

rules.name: The Traceable Severity Rule
rules.body: Severity is red / watch / none, each traceable to a sentence the parent said. No score, gauge, index, ring or sentiment bar exists or may be added.

rules.name: The Legible Grey Rule
rules.body: muted-strong is the floor for anything a user has to read — body copy, secondary lines, placeholders, disabled labels. muted is for decoration and non-essential metadata only. On this cream ramp muted never clears 3.9:1; the caregiver reading it is often presbyopic and always in a hurry.

rules.name: The Earned Serif Rule
rules.body: Newsreader appears only on care content: verbatim quotes, medicine names, the one hero line per screen, and the wordmark. It is never decoration, never a routine screen title, never sprinkled.

rules.name: The Verbatim Rule
rules.body: What the parent said renders exactly, wrapped in real quotation marks, never summarised, paraphrased, or restyled into a log line. Hindi/Marathi quotes carry a real lang attribute so they set in Plex Devanagari — and only when the text actually is in that language, since lang also changes the screen reader's voice.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Times, durations and counts take .tnum (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) so they never jitter as they tick.

rules.name: The One Thing Leads Rule
rules.body: Each screen has exactly one element that leads — the next dose on Home, the P1 alert when one is open (it outranks the dose), the quote on an observation. A stranger should know where to look in under a second.

rules.name: The Two Warm Shadows Rule
rules.body: No new shadow values. If a surface needs more presence, step its tone (surface → paper), thicken its border, or give it a left mark — do not invent a third drop shadow.

rules.name: The Lift Is Singular Rule
rules.body: --shadow-lift marks the one card that leads. Two lifted cards on one screen means neither leads.

rules.name: The One Left Mark Rule
rules.body: A card carries at most one left mark. Nested content that has its own spine (a QuoteBlock) sits in a card without one.

rules.name: The Handoff Rule
rules.body: The app never dials. A call action is a real <a href="tel:…"> styled as a Button, naming who it will dial. It is a handoff to the OS dialler, not an in-app call.

dos: Do give every status a shape and a text label first, then layer colour on top — and verify under achromatopsia emulation and in greyscale.
Do render parent quotes verbatim, in real quotation marks, sized as the most important text on the screen, with lang set only when the text really is Hindi or Marathi.
Do use muted-strong for anything the user must read; reserve muted for decoration and non-essential metadata.
Do show the literal rule string on alerts (rule: chest complaint with age over 40) under a P1/P2 badge, and keep the sentence "No interpretation, no diagnosis" on screen.
Do keep gated buttons visible with the reason adjacent ("2 left", "All three are mandatory"), and prefer the Warm Inert treatment over an opacity ghost.
Do style call actions as OS handoffs: real tel: links naming who they dial. Route in-app navigation through react-router Link, never a bare href.
Do load with skeletons in the final layout's shape; nothing may shift when data lands.
Do keep entrances at 340ms and state changes at 150ms on --ease-out / --ease-soft, and let prefers-reduced-motion collapse them.
Do keep touch targets ≥44px and times/counts in .tnum.
Do keep the sticky-footer bleed in step with <main>'s padding — 16px on a phone, 24px at lg:.
donts: Don't add a hue. One accent; emphasis is weight, border and whitespace. No green — "taken" is blue.
Don't invent a score, gauge, mood percentage, sentiment bar, wellbeing ring or index. Severity is red/watch/none, each traceable to a sentence. Feel the urge to add a gauge → add whitespace.
Don't add a fourth status mark, a fifth mobile tab, a third shadow, or a second left mark on one card.
Don't pass a Card emphasis outside none / border / rule / danger — an unrecognised value silently strips the card of all styling.
Don't use Newsreader outside care content (quotes, medicine names, the one hero line, the wordmark), or 11px for anything but labels and tab captions.
Don't use spinners, in-app dialling affordances, springy easings, or placeholder text of any kind (no lorem ipsum, no TODO).
Don't hardcode a hex. Every colour goes through a @theme token class.
Don't rename or delete @theme tokens; extend, don't replace.
